title: Define versioned context-budget profiles and token estimates

state.decision_rationale: Accepted as lossless, review, and structure profiles with explicit projections and declared heuristic budgets.

provenance.review_target: Reported 6.3 MB, 137715-line MKTCTX/3 packet; exact artifact not identified

feedback.verbatim: Add context-budget profiles. lossless is a good archival or retrieval-backed packet. It should not be the default raw prompt. Define manifest, review, query, and lossless-selection profiles. Per-file and packet token estimates would let the generator enforce a budget.
feedback.normalized_claim: Define explicit, versioned packet profiles for manifest-only, review, query-focused, and exact-selection use, with tokenizer-specific cost estimates and enforceable budgets.

current_behavior: The implemented ContextMode is lossless only; balanced, focused, and structure-only names fail explicitly as reserved.
Exact selected source is the default packet representation, with optional line-numbered citation views.
No tokenizer identity, token estimate, budget, relevance policy, or partial-source projection is implemented.
The design document already treats balanced, focused, and structure-only projections as deferred rather than silently lossy.

proposal.summary: Evaluate a profile layer that names selection and projection policies, declares tokenizer assumptions, and preserves an audit trail for every omitted or summarized body.
candidate_changes: Define manifest profile as interpretive metadata and outlines without source bodies.
Define review profile around policies, change provenance, exact changed files, and dependency outlines.
Define query profile only when explicit intent and evidence-backed relevance are available.
Rename or retain lossless-selection as the full exact selected-file profile.
Declare tokenizer provider, model or encoding version, per-file estimates, packet estimate, budget, and deterministic overflow policy.
Record projection decisions and omitted ranges so every loss is visible.
non_goals: Do not call a relevance-based packet query-focused without caller intent.
Do not use model-specific token counts without naming and versioning the tokenizer.
Do not silently truncate exact files to satisfy a budget.

questions: Are profiles part of MKTCTX core or separately versioned policy packages?
Which tokenizer or model determines budget compliance?
How should a review profile choose dependency outlines before verified edges exist?
Can one packet carry retrievable exact bodies outside the immediate prompt view?
What deterministic policy applies when mandatory content alone exceeds budget?
risks: Named profiles can create false expectations if their selection algorithms are underspecified.
Query profiles can omit counterevidence and create confident but incomplete answers.
Tokenizer drift makes cached estimates inaccurate.
Budget metadata itself adds size and complexity.
evidence_needed: Task suite comparing accuracy, recall, cost, and latency across proposed profiles.
Exact tokenizer counts for representative small and multi-megabyte packets.
Determinism tests for selection and overflow policies.
Prompt-injection and omitted-counterevidence evaluations for query-focused packets.
